title: Investigate and mitigate rate-limit amplification during blue/green private orchestrator upgrade
creator: Aisha Reddy
description:
Summary:
During a planned blue/green orchestrator upgrade in the EMEA private region on 2025-02-12 we observed an emergent amplification of control-plane API rate-limits that caused a cascade of backoffs and connection churn across private agents. Symptoms included increased API 429 responses from the control plane, simultaneous agent reconnect storms in multiple VPCs, and elevated request latencies for customer pods that rely on control-plane-side rollouts.

Impact:
- ~18 minutes of elevated tail latency for management-plane operations across 23 private customers in EMEA (no customer data loss).
- Automated rollbacks and canary promotions were delayed; two Dedicated customers reported degraded API responsiveness for management operations.
- Customer-facing inference traffic continued but some administrative operations (scale, config changes, rollouts) failed until mitigation.

What went wrong (summary of investigation):
- Blue/green upgrade introduced a subtle change in the orchestrator proxy: connection pooling was reinitialized on promotion instead of being gracefully handed over. That caused a spike in simultaneous new control-plane connections.
- A recent change to the control-plane rate-limiter (rate limit buckets tightened to reduce noisy-tenant impact) reduced headroom for bursty reconnects. The combination of many agents reconnecting and the tightened buckets produced 429 spikes.
- Agents had an aggressive jitter configuration for reconnects that biased towards short backoffs under transient failures, which further amplified the reconnect storm.
- DNS TTL for internal control-plane endpoints was briefly set to 10s in the staging config used for the rollout; this increased DNS traffic and contributed to request amplification under rapid reconnections.

Root cause (one-liner):
Mismatch between upgrade-driven connection churn, tighter rate-limiter settings, and agent backoff/jitter defaults (plus short DNS TTL) produced an amplified reconnect storm that exceeded control-plane rate buckets.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Reverted the orchestration proxy pool reinit code to the previous handover behavior (hotfix: gh-priv/ops#421).
- Temporarily relaxed rate-limiter burst thresholds for private regions (config flag: RATE_LIMIT_BURST=2x) to allow smoothing of reconnects.
- Increased DNS TTL for control-plane endpoints from 10s to 60s in the upgrade manifest.
- Pushed an outbound agent firmware toggle to increase exponential backoff min jitter by 3x for reconnections (agent feature-flag: agent_reconnect_jitter_soft).

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Permanent fix for orchestrator pool handover to avoid transient full reinitialization (owner: Liam Chen; ETA: 2025-03-03).
- Implement reconnection coordination: a centralized leader coordination window during promotions to batch reconnects (owner: Maya Gupta; ETA: 2025-03-12).
- Review and formalize rate-limiter policies for upgrade windows with a deploy-time override flag and automated safety gates (owner: Product - Jonah Park; ETA: 2025-03-07).
- Add preflight rollout checks: simulate agent reconnect patterns in canary before promotion (owner: SRE - Carlos Ortega; ETA: 2025-03-10).
- Update default agent backoff/jitter parameters and expose as configurable policy per deployment (owner: Agent Platform - Nadine Zhou; ETA: 2025-03-17).
- Add DNS configuration linting for upgrade manifests to prevent sub-30s TTL in production (owner: Release Eng - Priya Nair; ETA: 2025-03-01).
- Observability: add a composite alarm that triggers when 429 rate and reconnects exceed threshold for >5m (owner: Observability - Jae Kim; ETA: 2025-02-28).

Acceptance criteria for done:
- Pool handover patch merged and verified in staging with no reconnect spike during promotion.
- Rate-limiter deploy-time override exists and is documented in runbooks.
- Canary simulation test pipeline added to the upgrade workflow.
- Default agent backoff/jitter updated and rolled to <=50% of private fleet in a staged rollout.
